content: An annual wellness visit in the context of primary care and preventive medicine is a yearly appointment designed to create or update a personalized plan aimed at preventing disease and disability. This plan is tailored based on the patient’s current health status and individual risk factors. It is important to note that the annual wellness visit is not equivalent to a physical examination. Since January 2011, the Affordable Care Act has expanded Medicare coverage to include an Annual Wellness Visit (AWV) for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans. The primary focus of the AWV is to promote health and prevent disease by coordinating evidence-based preventive services. These services may include, but are not limited to, lipid and metabolic panels, pneumonia vaccinations, influenza vaccinations, and depression screenings. According to a policy statement published in the May 2019 edition of the AARP Public Policy Institute, supported by research from Camacho, Yao, and Anderson, there was a steady increase in the utilization of AWVs between 2011 and 2015. This rise in AWVs corresponded with an increase in the use of preventive services. More recent reviews have also linked the receipt of certain preventive care services to participation in annual wellness visits. Data indicates that 6% of Medicare beneficiaries in two separate cohorts had an annual wellness visit. Furthermore, in 2020, a large-scale quality improvement project resulted in 60% of patients receiving an annual wellness visit.
